bodies.name: 2012 VP113
bodies.axesStatus: Illustrative equal axes at the diameter its discoverers estimate for an assumed albedo of 0.10; not measured.
bodies.credit: Sheppard & Trujillo (2016), The Astronomical Journal 152, 221, Table 2: diameter 550 km for an assumed albedo of 0.10
bodies.shapeMeaning: Illustrative sphere 550 km across, the diameter Sheppard & Trujillo (2016, Table 2) estimate from its brightness for an assumed moderate albedo of 0.10. The size is not measured.
bodies.orientationMeaning: Illustrative ICRF north pole, arbitrary prime meridian and phase; no spin pole is published.
bodies.surfaceMeaning: Unmapped surface: the standard grid is a coordinate aid, not observed colour or terrain.
bodies.introduction: 2012 VP113 never comes closer to the Sun than about 80 au, and at the far end of its orbit it is about 450 au away. Its discoverers reported it in 2014 as a second Sedna-like body.
bodies.card: A Sedna-like body that never comes closer than about 80 au.
bodies.datasetSummary: A sphere 550 km across, the size its discoverers estimate for an assumed albedo.

bodies.name: Leleākūhonua
bodies.axesStatus: Equal axes at the occultation radius, which assumes a circular outline.
bodies.credit: Buie et al. (2020), The Astronomical Journal 159, 230: radius 110 +14/−10 km from the 2018 October 20 stellar occultation, assuming a circular profile
bodies.shapeMeaning: Sphere of radius 110 km (+14/−10 km), from one detection and one nearby non-detection of the 2018 October 20 stellar occultation (Buie et al. 2020). The radius assumes a circular outline; the shape is not measured.
bodies.orientationMeaning: Illustrative ICRF north pole, arbitrary prime meridian and phase; no spin pole is published.
bodies.surfaceMeaning: Unmapped surface: the standard grid is a coordinate aid, not observed colour or terrain.
bodies.introduction: Leleākūhonua never comes closer to the Sun than about 65 au, and its orbit reaches beyond 2,500 au. Its discoverers reported it as the third known member of the inner Oort cloud.
bodies.card: Found in 2015; its orbit reaches more than 2,500 au from the Sun.
bodies.datasetSummary: A sphere of radius 110 km, measured in a 2018 stellar occultation assuming a circular outline.
